api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

features.note: Both features are additive on review-v2 only. dense-128 raises the finding page from 32 to 128 and stays bounded by the 64 KiB body ceiling Core 0.10.0 serves, and reason-v1 adds a reason to each not_evaluated finding. A request without the header answers the published 32-finding, seven-key document; a header on review-v1, an unknown or repeated token, or an empty part is invalid_request, and a response that enabled a feature echoes the accepted set in the same header.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. v4 keeps v3's 13 top-level keys, the 44 MiB file limit and the canonical bytes, and raises the findings, resolutions and choices limits from 32 to 128 while allowing a reason on a not_evaluated finding; only the label v4 brings those limits, so a v1, v2 or v3 file keeps its 32-item caps and rejects reason. A writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4). The v4 contract ships in Web 0.4.0 and 0.4.1 and in Windows 0.6.0 and 0.6.1, not in Web 0.3.1 or Windows 0.5.1, which reject a v4 file; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

release.note: v0.10.1 is a translation release on top of v0.10.0. Paragraph regrouping of a context-mode answer into the source's paragraphs now compares a per-line share ratio, (answer line / answer total) / (source line / source total), over the whole segment instead of the 7.5% running-share bound and the six-line window, so a merge and a split at any distance and in either order are refused and a distant merge-plus-split answer keeps the model's own blank lines for a manual split. A merge is a line carrying at least 1.4 lines' worth of text that also stands 1.3 clear of the segment's median, or a line whose text matches its own source line plus a neighbour's; a split is a line left with at most 0.60 of its own text, or two adjacent lines carrying at most 0.65 each and 0.75 to 1.25 together, and a refusal needs both. The criteria were frozen in docs/eval/paragraph-layout-criteria.md before the change and scripts/verify_paragraph_regroup.py replays them (MY-359): 50,000 synthetic faithful answers at each of 10, 20 and 45 lines with plus or minus 35% per-line length noise reject 0.0000, the eight parametrised counterexamples fail on the previous guard and pass here, and the stored D-003 31- and 8-paragraph reproductions still regroup to the source's 45 paragraphs with their line sequence intact. The Web and Windows contract pins move to Web v0.4.1 (c1b9fd5c) and Windows v0.6.1 (4da26ba9), the patch releases of the two wuwaterm-manuscript-v4 clients, and contracts/web-ref.txt, contracts/windows-ref.txt, the split revisions of contracts/ci-source-epochs.json and the matching assertions in tests/test_ci_source_epoch.py carry them together; no Core API version, OpenAPI shape or translation request changes with the pins, and the OpenAPI document moves only its info.version. The dictionary, the builder and the terms.db it produces are those of v0.10.0. The snapshot frozen in this tag names Web v0.4.1 and Telegram v0.4.0 for the installer, so an install from the v0.10.1 tag needs no Web override; Telegram v0.4.1, the release built on this Core, was published after the tag and is recorded on main, and an install from the tag names it with WUWATERM_TELEGRAM_VERSION=v0.4.1 or runs from main. CI run 44692505542 passed on dd23830, the dry run 44694133479 built every artifact without pushing images, the draft release run 44694379176 built the published assets, and the release-triggered run 44694763373 promoted the image tags.

previous_release.note: v0.10.0 is a review and translation release. review-v2 gives every mapped region its own claim and allocation step: when the occurrences a region holds cannot cover the mentions competing for them, it credits none of those mentions instead of whichever one a sweep reaches first, a partial assignment is the largest one rather than the first one found, an inflection never answers a competing official form, a numbering dot no longer ends a sentence where review-v2 pairs them (segmentation-v1 keeps the boundary it publishes), an occurrence enclosed by a longer official form is not a standalone hit unless the source claims that longer term, a lowercase spelling of a capitalized official term is an ordinary word, and a derived name surface asserts no constraint. The CJK matcher basis label moves to wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v8, so stored resolution contexts and saved v3 segment results carrying -v7 go stale by the existing freshness rule and are re-reviewed. POST /v1/reviews accepts a 64 KiB body instead of 32 KiB, and review-v2 callers may opt into dense-128 and reason-v1 with X-WuwaTerm-Review-Features under an exact grammar that echoes the accepted set back. Regrouping a context-mode answer into the source's paragraphs refuses a crossing paragraph break and a merge-plus-split line layout and keeps the model's own blank lines. Every LLM request byte, term lock and reference list is identical to 0.9.2, and the builder and the terms.db it produces are unchanged, so an install keeps the database it built. The Web and Windows contract pins move to Web v0.4.0 (7cfbc4d5) and Windows v0.6.0 (eaceb8bb), the two consumers of wuwaterm-manuscript-v4; no Core API version or OpenAPI shape changes with the pins. CI run 44599508979 passed on 67e27da, the draft release run 44602177160 built the assets, and the release-triggered run 44602964761 promoted the image tags. Kept as history after v0.10.1; the release and its assets are still published. v0.9.2 and earlier remain on the release page.

release.note: v0.4.1 pins the published Core 0.10.1 wheel, whose SHA-256 0b38d3bcf40ee4658e2fdb4423eb5f99620e9d9262614224b5a737aa4cb0529d is the core_binding this bundle records, with core_source_commit dd238303 and the compatibility it declares exact (OCI index sha256:5c68d0d7e45ce67928ddb66c84a83cb75afbdd8b1faef2166c9363dad7768f63, manifest sha256:f94cf6fae5b79388f3c2578e476caa088df9e79604d161fb077163eed27b05c7, config sha256:501746ea792ad53e84116fdbd14e4fe2214f1c68f986e35ad0922389dbadd84e, built by image-bundle run 44697588205). It is a patch release on v0.4.0. The code change (#43) makes a failed shared-pointer send visible instead of silent: both send branches of _point_to_shared_result go through _notice_failed_delivery, so a reuser, including a waiter served the pointer after the same content was queued, receives the failure notice with its resend button while the job stays undelivered, and pressing it or submitting the same content again sends the stored report without another model call. Automatic retry narrows to a send that provably never left: _is_presend_network_error walks the cause chain and accepts only httpx.ConnectError and httpx.ProxyError, so ReadError, RemoteProtocolError, WriteError, a bare NetworkError, BadRequest, Forbidden and TimedOut are not retried, and no retry happens once any chunk has reached the chat. The failure notice splits by outcome: the existing notice says the result was not delivered, and a new uncertain notice says Telegram may have received it and a resend may duplicate, which is the path a ConnectTimeout takes because python-telegram-bot 22.8 raises TimedOut for it rather than NetworkError. Seven test cases cover the two files. The release-prep change (#44) is the Core pin, the package metadata and the docs that describe it, and the tag push produced no duplicate CI run: the only run on this commit that the tag started is the release run itself.

Every LLM request byte, term lock and reference list is identical to Core 0.9.2, and the builder and its terms.db are unchanged, so an existing install keeps the database it built. release.note: v0.6.1 is a maintenance release on v0.6.0 (#32). A term-group place taken from a reopened v3 or v4 manuscript has no review basis for this session yet, so it is a saved result: the group reads 待核对依据 and 已保存，尚未核对当前依据 instead of 已核, the 待处理 filter lists it rather than hiding it behind a confirmed status, occurrence rows, the 按出现顺序 rows and the occurrence detail badge carry the same note where they would otherwise say 约束已核, and a recorded conflict still stays a decision to make. Group status never confirms while any of its places is a saved result, and saved_count says how many are. Grouping only reads the records, so the saved report, its per-occurrence spans and its distribution are unchanged and the first live check restores 已核; the file formats and the service requirements are those of 0.6.0, HTTP API v1 with review-v2 for manuscript review. previous_release.note: v0.6.0 reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v4 and adds term grouping and per-occurrence work in the review panel (#30). Findings, resolutions and choices per manuscript or segment rise from 32 to 128, a not_evaluated finding can carry a structured reason, and the review request declares X-WuwaTerm-Review-Features: dense-128,reason-v1; a writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4), so a manuscript that does not need v4 keeps its lower format and old clients keep opening it. The panel groups the occurrences of one term by form and candidate with a pending filter and reads "another N segments to review" and the not-evaluated reason, per-occurrence replace and revise work in the group, the editor fixes Enter, CRLF and a bare CR concatenation and keeps the caret and selection of a rejected edit, an unreviewed short segment shows as pending again instead of reviewed, and a text that cannot be split reliably after translation gets a jump entry. It requires HTTP API v1, and manuscript review also needs review-v2. Windows 0.5.1 and Web 0.3.1 reject v4 files. Kept as history after v0.6.1; the release and its assets are still published. v0.5.1 and earlier remain on the release page.

release.note: v0.4.1 is a patch release on v0.4.0 (#47). A term-group place taken from a reopened v3 or v4 manuscript stays pending (待处理, shown as 已保存，尚未核对当前词典与规则) until a live review request shows that Core's dictionary and matcher basis still equal the saved basis, so the to-do filter lists that group instead of hiding it behind a confirmed status; a saved place is pending unless it is a confirmed conflict, no group reads confirmed while one of its places sits on a saved result, and a group counts the places that do (savedCount). Choices, renderings and the per-place detail stay untouched, and the v3 and v4 file formats, the BFF response shape, the /v1 proxy, the database schema, the dependencies, the hosting configuration and the Core and Windows contract pins are those of 0.4.0. The release prep moves package.json and package-lock.json to 0.4.1 with no other version field moved, adds a Version 0.4.1 section to docs/self-hosting.md whose publication steps use v0.4.1, and reflows docs/sites.md line 150 to the width of its paragraph with no wording change. The published root and prefix archives match their manifests and SHA256SUMS. v0.4.0 and its assets remain published under previous_release.
